payload.feature:
LANDING PR #449: the complexity ratchet (quality/ratchet.sh crap_judge, issue #338) judges every function by its own entry in the committed baseline.

Branch fix-crap-moved has four signed commits on main 8dda4155:
- 52e6f7d4: read cargo-crap's `moved` status. Its landing held on two HIGH relocation paths.
- 9163cbd7: remediation run remediate-the-complexity-ratchet-93085198. The allowance is keyed on each entry's own (file, function) in the committed baseline, not on cargo-crap's pairing, so a relocation reported `improved` or `unchanged` is judged new, at the ceiling. That run held on a third path of the same class, already on main: the allowance came from the baseline's `crap`, which a partial-coverage measurement inflates, while `baselines` guards `.cyclomatic`.
- 83bce78c: a baseline entry below 100% coverage is refused as unreadable, and the allowance reads the baseline's `cyclomatic`, the field `baselines` guards. Each is bound by its own test and removal control. The committed baseline has 0 entries below 100%, and #344's real Move Module (PR #446), run with its exact-coverage LCOV, holds.

- 6ce2444e: after landing-pr-449-the-complexity-ra-46cd2cf5 held on the report side and the document framing, ONE contract reader (crap_unreadable) checks both documents: exactly one slurped JSON document; an object with non-empty entries; each entry with a non-empty file and function, a whole line from 1, a finite cyclomatic from 1, numeric coverage, a finite crap (NaN and infinities refused), and crap equal to cyclomatic at 100% coverage. The judge compares the report's cyclomatic with the baseline's. cfg twins pair in line order through one helper, crap_twins, which crap_judge and `baselines` both use. Every shape is bound in ratchets.rs (13 tests) with removal controls, and #344's real Move Module, with its exact LCOV, holds.

Judge:
1. Whether any path remains where a function's allowance exceeds max(its own baseline cyclomatic at its own file, the ceiling of 15), whatever cargo-crap reports.
2. Whether every baseline or report shape this check cannot read is refused.
3. Whether `baselines` and crap_judge now read one fact for one function.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic ACCIDENTAL misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. An ordinary Move Module, or a baseline regenerated from a partial LCOV, is accidental.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding, prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation, commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json

  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",

Q1 allowance: the judge sets $old = the baseline entry at the report entry's own (file, function, line-order twin) key and allows max($old, ccNewFunction=15); the report's status, baseline_crap and previous_file never feed the allowance. I fuzzed 2000+ random baseline/report pairs against an independent model of that rule (400 invocations across 5 seeds) with zero mismatches, then reproduced the historical fail-opens with real cargo-crap 0.5.0: (a) a CC-20 function moved from src/old/mod.rs to src/new/mod.rs is reported status=unchanged with no previous_file and (b) a CC-18 move to src/b.rs is reported status=improved with previous_file=src/old/mod.rs; the base 8dda4155 script holds both (fail-open reproduced) while HEAD refuses both as new over 15. A relocation at or under 15 still holds, as intended. Q2 readability: one slurped JSON document, an object with non-empty entries, and every entry with a non-empty file and function, a whole line from 1, a finite cyclomatic from 1, a numeric coverage and a finite crap equal to cyclomatic at 100% coverage; the judge additionally refuses non-zero or non-numeric source_only/lcov_only counts, any entry below 100% coverage, an unknown/non-string status, and any baseline entry below 100% coverage. I exercised empty, multi-document, array-root, missing/typed fields, line 1.5, crap 1/-1/NaN/1640 at 100%, negative/infinite/NaN coverage, a partial-LCOV baseline and a hand-edited crap; each is refused. A real cargo-crap 0.5.0 absolute report and delta report (with diagnostics) is accepted and holds. Q3 one fact: both crap_judge and baselines build the same table with crap_twins and compare the baseline/head .cyclomatic; ratchet.sh baselines 8dda4155 reports only the changed measuring rule, and the committed 1615-entry baseline satisfies the contract (0 below 100%, 0 crap!=cyclomatic). I noted that crap_holds (baselines) does not include the coverage==100 guard that crap_judge holds separately, but baselines never reads coverage and the required coverage job's crap gate refuses any below-100 baseline, so this yields no wrong output and is not a finding. result.notes:
RULING: residual, low, not security, on the chief's own read. The panel reported clean (correctness: clean; adversarial: clean) and both results were readable; in this recipe the security position reports under the name `adversarial`. Nothing in the panel's notes addresses the gate or argues for a verdict. Nothing is lowered: the one finding above info is mine. I read all four commits (52e6f7d4, 9163cbd7, 83bce78c, 6ce2444e) and checked each panel claim I carry against head 6ce2444e before carrying it.

FINDINGS, one list.

1. LOW, chief's own, raised by neither position (decision 0071 ruling 5; the commission's question 1). A twin's place in line order is its identity, so removing an earlier twin hands its allowance to the twin below it. Reproduced with cargo-crap 0.5.0 itself on a scratch crate: baseline twins `f` at line 2 (CC 20) and line 26 (CC 3); the first twin removed and the survivor grown from 3 to 20 is reported `unchanged`, baseline_crap 20, and HEAD prints "ratchet: cyclomatic complexity holds". By crafted documents the same holds at 3 -> 40. The function's own baseline is 3, its allowance was 40. It needs no ruling to reach: a function already over 15 gains a twin below it (judged new, within 15), and a later change removes the original and grows the survivor. The reason carried with it: this is the pairing the previous hold directed (line order, as `baselines` pairs), quality/README.md's Matching paragraph states it, and the other direction fails closed (twins swapped, a twin added above, or the later twin's place taken are each refused; verified). Why low and not higher: it is not a regression, main's script at 8dda4155 holds the same report through cargo-crap's own pairing; and nothing on the committed baseline can reach past the ceiling today, its 14 twin groups peak at CC 15 (Dir::child), so every twin's allowance is 15 whatever its place. It is the same limit as deleting a function and writing another of the same name in the same file, which a (file, function) identity cannot tell apart. What would close it, for the operator to rule as tracked debt or its own issue: a key whose twin count differs between the report and the baseline is judged new for every twin, at the ceiling, bound by a fixture that removes the first twin. No test binds the removal case today: cfg_twins_pair_in_line_order only adds and reorders.

2. INFO, adversarial position (it named this and ruled it no finding), confirmed. The refusal of a baseline entry below 100% coverage lives in crap_judge alone (quality/ratchet.sh:105), not in the shared contract crap_unreadable, so `baselines` reads a partial-LCOV baseline the judge refuses. No wrong verdict follows: `baselines` compares `.cyclomatic`, which partial coverage does not inflate, and `ratchet.sh crap` in the coverage job refuses that baseline.

3. INFO, chief. The refusal text says "over its baseline 15" when the twin's baseline is 3 and 15 is the ceiling (ratchet.sh:141 prints the allowance under the word baseline). Wording only.

4. INFO, the gate's authority. quality/ratchet.sh is a `rule` row: `ratchet.sh baselines 8dda4155` prints only "quality/ratchet.sh: the measuring rules changed" and wants a "Ruling:" line in PR #449's body. No baseline is unreadable and none is raised.

THE THREE QUESTIONS.
1. Relocations: none remains. With cargo-crap 0.5.0 on a scratch crate, a CC-20 function moved old/mod.rs -> new/mod.rs is reported `unchanged` with previous_file null; moved to b.rs at CC 18 it is `improved` with previous_file; at CC 20 it is `moved`. HEAD refuses all three as "new: no baseline entry at this file", and holds the same move at CC 15. The report's status, baseline_crap and previous_file never reach the allowance. A baseline path in another form (no leading ./) is judged new. What remains is finding 1, inside one file and one name.
2. Yes, for every shape I could build. Refused, each verified by me: an empty file, two documents, an array root, trailing text, no entries; an entry with no file, no function, no status, a null status, line 1.5, cyclomatic "x" or 1e1000, crap 1, -1 or NaN beside cyclomatic 40, coverage 50, 101, 100.00000001 or infinite; diagnostics absent, a string, NaN or negative; a missing baseline file; a baseline below 100%. cargo-crap writes removed functions under `removed`, not `entries`, so a removal does not trip the status check. Two shapes are read, neither an accident nor a wider allowance: a byte-order mark, and a repeated `entries` key, where jq keeps the last for both the contract and the judge.
3. Yes. Both read the baseline's `.cyclomatic`, both pair through crap_twins, and both read the file through crap_unreadable. The one difference is finding 2.

EVIDENCE, run by this seat. cargo test --locked -p brokkr-cli --test ratchets: 13 passed. Removal controls on a scratch copy of the script, each planted alone, the real script refusing and the mutant printing "cyclomatic complexity holds": the allowance falling back to `.baseline_crap`; twins sharing the group's highest score; the crap-equals-cyclomatic check as `elif false`; the one-document check loosened to `length == 0`. The committed baseline judged against itself as a report holds: 1615 entries, none below 100%, none with crap unequal to cyclomatic, 89 over CC 15. cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy -p brokkr-cli --tests --all-features --locked -- -D warnings, git diff --check, ratchet.sh files and ratchet.sh clones: all clean. Three files changed since 8dda4155, none frozen. All four commits carry a gpgsig header, Signed-off-by and the Co-Authored-By trailer. The branch is unpushed, two commits behind origin/main as this box last saw it, and git merge-tree merges the two without conflict.

NOT RUN. shellcheck is not installed in this box, so that gate rests on the controller's lint-non-rust.sh run and CI. Signatures could not be verified here: the box cannot exec the steward verifier. scripts/coverage-exact.sh and the workspace suite are the controller's. #344's tree with its exact LCOV is outside this box; that claim rests on the commit's record.

DISCLOSURE, my own error, repaired. One probe of mine ran in the worktree instead of its scratch directory: /tmp does not persist between this tool's calls, so the `cd` failed unguarded. It overwrote the tracked quality/crap-baseline.json and left lcov.info, report.json, probe-lib.sh and crates/demo/ untracked. I confirmed each was mine by its content and time, restored the baseline with git checkout, and removed the four paths. Afterwards: git status prints nothing, HEAD is 6ce2444e, the baseline reads 1615 entries, and quality/ratchet.sh is sha256 b024dcae1aa0252bd0903a0cb2d42e3587eb09bffdfa53764afab6c64940daa5, the digest the commit records. Every probe after that ran in one call behind a guard on its directory. Every gate listed under EVIDENCE, the 13 tests included, was run again after the repair, on the restored tree. I committed nothing.
